name: Beef Birria
desc: Chuck and short ribs rubbed with warm spices overnight, then braised in a guajillo chile and tomato broth until fall-apart tender.

source.title: Beef Birria
source.evidence: Chef John's Allrecipes recipe: every ingredient and amount matches (2 1/2 lb chuck, 3 short ribs, 7 guajillos, 4 cups broth, 1/4 cup white vinegar, 1 tbsp honey), and the steps and chef's notes are the same text.

ingredients.raw: 1 (1 inch) piece fresh ginger, thinly sliced

steps: Cut the chuck in half, then cut each half into 3- to 4-inch pieces. Cut each short rib through the middle, down to the bone.

Put the chuck and short ribs in a soup pot and season with the kosher salt, oregano, black pepper, cumin, cinnamon, and cloves. Toss for 2-3 minutes until evenly coated. Cover and refrigerate for at least 6 hours or overnight.
Snip the stems off the guajillo chiles with scissors, slice them open, and shake out and discard the seeds.
Heat the olive oil in a saucepan over medium heat. Add the chiles and toss in the hot oil for about 30 seconds. Add the onion, garlic, and ginger and toss to combine.
Add the tomatoes and water and bring to a boil. Reduce the heat to medium-low and simmer for 30 minutes.
Turn off the heat and puree the mixture as smooth as possible with an immersion blender, or in batches in a countertop blender.
Take the pot of meat out of the refrigerator. Strain the chile puree into the pot through a large mesh strainer, pressing on the solids. Add the chicken broth, vinegar, bay leaves, and honey.

Bring to a boil, then reduce the heat to medium-low. Simmer gently, stirring occasionally, until the meat is fall-apart tender, 3 to 4 hours. Add water or broth as needed to keep it brothy. Skim the fat off the top and save it for birria queso tacos if you like.
To serve, put a few chunks of beef in each bowl and spoon the cooking liquid over the top. Sprinkle with white onion and cilantro and squeeze lime over the top.
tips: Use about 1 tsp kosher salt per pound of meat.
Other dried chiles such as ancho, pasilla, or California work in place of guajillo, and water with chicken bouillon powder can stand in for the broth.
Serve the beef in large chunks or shred it with a fork. Goat or lamb prepared the same way also works well.
